title.narrative: Emergency Education Response for Conflict-Affected Children (Including Girls and Children with Disabilities) in Raya Kobo and Guba Lafto Woredas in North Wollo Zone Amhara Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtDevelopment through Adult and Non-Formal Education (DANFE), a women-led national NGO with over two decades of experience in Ethiopia, proposes a 12-month emergency education intervention targeting 5,600 out-of-school children—including 560 children with disabilities—and 160 teachers and Facilitators in the conflict-affected woredas of Raya Kobo and Guba Lafto, North Wollo Zone. The project aims to restore access to inclusive, quality education services disrupted by recent and ongoing conflict affected children, addressing both the immediate learning needs and the long-term recovery of vulnerable children. The intervention aligns with Ethiopia’s Education Cluster priorities and the Humanitarian Response Plan, with a strong emphasis on gender equity and disability inclusion. The project is structured around four integrated components. First, it will deliver Accelerated and Catch-Up Education through the proven Speed School model, enabling out-of-school children to complete four years of primary education within a single academic year. this will be implements in 14 newly established and rehabilitate Temporary Learning Centers (TLCs) located within ten existing school compounds, averaging 10 class room per site. Second, the project will provide essential teaching and learning materials to both students and teachers, including school kits with notebooks, pens, and pencils. Third, 140 teachers and 20 Supervisors will receive comprehensive training on content delivery, trauma-informed pedagogy, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Social Emotional Learning (SEL), and inclusive education approaches. Finally, children with disabilities will receive tailored support, including assistive devices, individualized learning plans, and access to inclusive classrooms. To ensure a safe, protective, and inclusive learning environment, each TLC 52% will be constructed from locally available materials and the rest 42% will rehabilitate with minor maintenance to functionalized the current class room. These facilities will include gender-sensitive WASH components, such as separate latrines for boys and girls, handwashing stations, and menstrual hygiene management (MHM) materials. A community-based approach will be applied throughout implementation, engaging Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), local education offices, education clusters and community leaders in planning, mobilization, and oversight. The project will utilize routine monitoring tools, including school visits, teacher feedback sessions, and community meetings, to track progress and make adaptive adjustments. By the end of the project, DANFE will have re-established access to quality education for thousands of displaced and vulnerable children, strengthened teacher capacity to respond to crisis-related learning and psychosocial needs, and improved community resilience through inclusive and sustainable learning spaces. Certification of learning outcomes and coordination with education authorities will support smooth transitions into formal education pathways. The holistic design ensures the intervention not only addresses immediate educational disruptions but also lays the foundation for long-term recovery and development in the conflict-affected communities of North Wollo.ltbrgtlt/pgt
